tldr: Azure API Management v2 can have different outbound-IP behavior from classic tiers; review backend allowlists and use a NAT Gateway if you need predictable egress.
Azure SQL Database preview adds database-level managed identity, including federated identity credentials, for access to Blob Storage and Data Lake Storage.
DoorDash reports cutting grocery reorder latency from 16 seconds to 2 by combining batch inference with deterministic checks—a useful pattern for keeping user-facing AI flows responsive.

top.title: APIM v2 outbound IPs differ from classic tiers; NAT Gateway restores predictability
top.summary: The guidance explains that Standard v2 and Premium v2 outbound networking differs from classic API Management tiers, where backends may rely on dedicated outbound IPs for allowlisting. A NAT Gateway can provide predictable outbound IP addresses for v2 deployments.
top.why: Check backend firewall allowlists before migrating or deploying APIM v2, and include a NAT Gateway in the design if those backends require stable source IPs.

top.title: Azure SQL preview adds database-level managed identity for external data access
top.summary: Azure SQL Database can now use a user-assigned managed identity at the individual database level, including a federated identity credential, to access Blob Storage and Data Lake Storage Gen2 through external tables and OPENROWSET.
top.why: This gives you a way to separate data-access identities by database instead of sharing credentials broadly; assess it for designs that query files from Azure SQL.

top.title: Azure MCP Server 3.0 is generally available with Terraform support
top.summary: Azure MCP Server 3.0 is generally available, expanding how AI agents and developer tools interact with Azure through the Model Context Protocol and adding Azure Terraform infrastructure-as-code capabilities.
top.why: If you are giving agents Azure management tools, evaluate the GA server against your deployment and access controls before allowing it to act on infrastructure.

top.title: Front Door Premium WAF's HTTP DDoS ruleset reaches general availability
top.summary: The HTTP-layer DDoS ruleset is now generally available for Azure Front Door Premium Web Application Firewall, adding protection beyond static controls such as IP filters and fixed rate limits.
top.why: Review the ruleset for internet-facing Front Door workloads where application-layer traffic spikes could otherwise cause downtime.

top.title: Large OS Disk Encryption is GA for Confidential VM migrations
top.summary: Large OS Disk Encryption is generally available for Azure Confidential VM migration scenarios, enabling larger production workloads to move with their OS disks fully protected.
top.why: Revisit confidential-computing migration plans that were blocked by OS disk size or encryption requirements.

also.title: Azure Cloud HSM adds hardware-originated audit logging
also.summary: Azure Cloud HSM hardware audit logs provide security and operations teams with verifiable evidence for monitoring, compliance reporting, and forensic investigations.

top.title: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft and Anthropic back a shared AI-crawling opt-out signal
top.summary: OpenAI says it will honor a shared robots.txt signal so website operators can express AI-training preferences to participating providers, with Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic also reported as supporters.
top.why: For products that collect or use web content, track how the standard is implemented and make crawler behavior and training-data policies consistent across providers.

also.title: Google reports its first AI response from a satellite running Gemma 4
also.summary: Google says a satellite equipped with a Tensor Processing Unit ran Gemma 4 and transmitted a response to Earth, an early demonstration rather than a production service.

top.title: Google's PageBreak AI security agent found more than 500 XSS bugs
top.summary: Google says PageBreak, an agent using Gemini models, uncovered more than 500 cross-site scripting vulnerabilities across its web applications since entering full operation in January. It reports findings only after deterministic validators reproduce the exploit against a running application.
top.why: When assessing AI-assisted security tools, look for the same validation step: agent-generated findings need reproducible evidence before they enter a remediation queue.

top.title: Netflix treats GPU reliability as a distributed-systems problem
top.summary: Netflix describes a reliability platform for large-scale GPU training and inference that combines layered health checks, automated remediation, and fault-tolerant training to keep work running through hardware failures.
top.why: Design GPU services around detecting and recovering from hardware faults, rather than assuming a healthy Kubernetes cluster means the model workload is healthy.

top.title: DoorDash cut grocery reorder latency from 16 seconds to 2 with AI agents
top.summary: DoorDash says it reduced grocery reorder latency from 16 seconds to 2 by precomputing recurring needs with batch LLM inference, validating selections deterministically, and resolving current catalog items separately; shopping-list views doubled and order rate rose about 34%.
top.why: For latency-sensitive AI features, consider moving repeatable work to batch inference and using deterministic validation so each live request needs fewer model calls.
